newsitem.title: USA: Clinton warns Bosnian Serbs against retaliation.
newsitem.headline: Clinton warns Bosnian Serbs against retaliation.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton sternly warned the Bosnian Serbs on Tuesday not to retaliate for a recent swoop on suspected war criminals, saying this would be a "grave mistake".
"They have no call to take any retaliatory action and it would be a grave mistake to do so," Clinton told reporters at the start of a White House meeting with congressional leaders.

Clinton made his remarks following a bomb explosion early on Tuesday morning outside the apartment of an international monitor in Bosnian Serb-controlled territory, the second straight night the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) was targeted.

The blast caused no injuries but shattered windows of an apartment building in the northwestern town of Banja Luka, the mission said in Sarajevo. The bombing heightened concern about a possible nationalist backlash against international staff working in Serb territory.

Clinton was asked at the start of a budget meeting with lawmakers whether he was worried about the possibility of a Bosnian Serb backlash following a NATO arrest operation last week against two Serbs indicted for war crimes. One man was arrested and a second shot dead in a gun battle.

"Well I am concerned about it, of course I am. But the representatives of the Serbs signed the Dayton agreement," he said. "The Dayton agreement says that if someone is charged with a war crime, they should be turned over (for) trial."
"They have clearly not complied with that provision of the Dayton agreement. They have made no effort to help us bring in these people," Clinton added.
Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, who attended the White House meeting, also complained about a lack of compliance with the Dayton peace accords by all parties to the agreement.

"They are not opening up their railroads. They are not opening up their airports. They're not connecting communications," the Mississippi Republican said. "There are a whole raft of areas where they need to be making progress."
The arrest operation was carried out on Thursday near the northwestern town of Prijedor by British special forces acting on orders from North Atlantic Treaty Organisation commanders.
Tensions are running high in Bosnia's Serb republic against international monitors in Serb territory following the NATO swoop.
On Sunday night, a bomb destroyed an OSCE pickup truck outside offices belonging to the OSCE and the United Nations mission in the eastern town of Zvornik. No one was injured in that explosion.
